newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM softens stand on exiled prince.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM softens stand on exiled prince.

text.p: Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen on Tuesday softened his strong protest against the return of exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh, saying he would welcome the prince with flowers if he is granted a royal pardon.

"Prince Sirivudh has the right to return to Cambodia safely and I warmly welcome him after King (Norodom Sihanouk) decrees that he has granted him amnesty," Hun Sen said in a speech at the Social Affairs Ministry.
"If Sirivudh is short of money for a return ticket, ask me, I will buy a ticket for him," Hun Sen said.
He said he would buy a first class ticket if necessary and bring 5,000 flowers to the airport to greet him.
The comments marked a sharp change from the second prime minister's comments at the weekend, when he vowed to call out tanks and troops if necessary to prevent Sirivudh's plane from landing.
Sirivudh, who is the king's half-brother, was exiled to France nearly one year ago after being accused of plotting to assassinate Hun Sen. He was sentenced in absentia to 10 years' jail.
The prince has since vowed to return to Cambodia, infuriating Hun Sen and driving a wedge between Hun Sen and co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who has supported Sirivudh's return.
Hun Sen said he referred to calling out tanks and troops to ensure a smooth arrest if Sirivudh returned without an amnesty.
"If he comes (without amnesty), we must take him into custody," Hun Sen said of Sirivudh, adding that unspecified "opposition forces" might have tried to block the arrest at the airport.
Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan said on Tuesday his guerrillas would protect the prince if he returned.
The Khmer Rouge, who ruled the country by terror from 1975 to 1979, have been fighting the government that emerged after U.N.-run general elections in 1993.
Diplomats and analysts puzzled over Hun Sen's change of tone.
"Perhaps it is to calm things down, or perhaps he is just taunting Sirivudh," said one diplomat. "It is difficult to say."
